dialogue.content: gave up after ten minutes and made tea instead.
followed some instructions to assemble a thing. worked first time.
sharpened everything that could be sharpened.
when I've got the steps in front of me I do the steps. I don't ask why any of them are there, and I couldn't tell you afterwards.
not one of them. I can do it and not know it.
found an old recording I'd forgotten making.
swapped one component for a nearly identical one.
spent the session on a bit nobody will ever notice.
wrote a list of things to learn. filed the list.
did it badly on purpose to see what happened.
worked out a small setting on my own. took five minutes.
cleared the workspace properly for the first time in months.
tried the thing everyone recommends. hated it.
the things I can still do years later are the ones I worked out unaided, badly, over far too long. the course material went completely, and quickly.
months. and there was a lot of it.
counted how many of these I actually own.
did a slow warm-up and nothing else.
recorded it on my phone to hear it back.
ordered a part and forgot what it was for.
did half an hour standing up for no reason.
compared two versions for far too long.
